claimFindingKind.description: The kind of a claim_check finding.

forbiddenContextCategory.description: Never accepted, whatever a caller sends. Credentials, wallets, result rows and bind values do not enter model context.

oneOf.description: Sent once, before any answer text. Carries the context preview.
oneOf.title: start

oneOf.description: A reviewable editor diff, pinned to the document revision and hash it was generated from. Applying it changes the editor buffer only. A multi-part proposal (multiPart: true) pins each part to its own editor, revision and hash, and carries the text in parts.
oneOf.title: proposal

oneOf.description: Kiwi only: a model turn is starting. Sent before each step of a request that may make read-only lookups.
oneOf.title: plan_step

oneOf.description: Kiwi only: the model asked for a reviewed read-only catalog lookup. It runs as the requesting user, on the requesting target.
oneOf.title: tool_call

oneOf.description: Kiwi only: how a lookup ended, with its Execution id. Counts and sizes only; the rows never appear in the stream.
oneOf.title: tool_result

oneOf.description: Kiwi only: steps, lookups, tokens, bytes and wall time spent against their limits, and which limits are exhausted.
oneOf.title: budget

oneOf.description: Kiwi explain actions only: the nodes and edges read from the source, the catalog and the scheduler, each edge labelled with its evidence (source, inferred, catalog or scheduler), plus a Mermaid rendering.
oneOf.title: lineage

oneOf.description: Kiwi answers other than the explain actions (protocol 1.4), plain diagnoses, plain explanations of supplied source and of a supplied plan, and edits (edit_description and proposal_directive, in a revision only): the harness's check of the answer's verifiable claims against the request's lookups: session role, a session's own cursor taken for the statement that took its lock (lock_origin), a session's reported SQL_ID called what it last ran, or a cursor's cumulative counters said of one execution (session_cursor), Oracle MOD arithmetic, where a change belongs, a larger limit for a complete result (next_check_cap), history from current state (history_claim), a role grant said not to reach stored code beside invoker's rights, AUTHID CURRENT_USER said to move compile-time privilege checks to the invoker, or a system or object privilege called a role (rights_model), citations that cannot support their statement (evidence_reference: a lookup not made, a failed one, or one not about the object named, by owner and name together, or a line given as a named member's first line, or as one of its lines, that the returned source rows place elsewhere) and next steps with no stated Unknown (next_check_unknown), a table or object called the only one in its schema with something when no lookup listed and read every table there, or the only matching object after listings filtered by type or beside other matching objects returned (schema_scope), a table change said to be needed to record a label a text column read can hold, or edits at every call site past the source read (required_change), a job with failed runs said to need no intervention, whatever source was read (job_intervention), a later run's outcome predicted from the scheduler's state or history (future_outcome), code no lookup located, named by what it does, said to be invisible or not to exist when searches returned no rows (absence_inference); a member said to be read that the source lookups did not return (read_coverage), a comparison with a member read in part, named or as its neighbours, or a statement about every member of a unit read in part, past the lines returned (read_scope), a band check said to fire on values an earlier rule's band, inside it, already rejects (band_reachability), a kiwi-next-checks block that could not be read (next_checks_block); for a plain explanation, a remedy its task asks for and the answer does not give (missing_remedy), or what the transaction holds when a later change fails before a handler that swallows the error, not stated, or a rollback after a re-raise denied without telling an unhandled top-level call from a catching caller (transaction_state), or two statements of one block with no handler of their own said to fail in one call, or the later to run after the earlier fails (control_flow); for a plain plan explanation, INTERNAL_FUNCTION round a column attributed to a bind conversion or an unshown bind datatype (plan_expression); and, for an edit, prose saying the proposal kept comments it removes, or changed only one thing (edit_description), or a proposal carrying text written as an instruction to the assistant from untrusted source (proposal_directive). Every kind is in definitions.claimFindingKind. All findings share one revision. stage is answer or revised; action is none, revise, skipped:<bound>, skipped:bounded_fallback (findings in the harness's own answer, which is never revised), revision_failed:<reason>, settled:corrected or settled:bounded_fallback (revised-stage findings that stood after the one revision, or answer-stage findings in a Kiwi diagnosis written as a bound ended the request: the harness corrected or withheld the flagged statements, or wrote the bounded diagnosis in the answer's place; no model call), or check_failed:<error>. unchecked (1.5) lists claims a check recognised but could not compute, which are neither confirmed nor corrected. A finding is a check of wording and scope, not a verdict. A revision is a step of the same request, within its remaining wall time.
oneOf.title: claim_check

oneOf.description: Answers with a claim_check, to clients announcing protocol 1.4 or later: the text that follows replaces draft, the last text streamed, which the client removes from the answer. A Kiwi claim revision's draft is all the text streamed, the notes between lookups included, so the revised answer replaces them too. With restored, a revision did not finish and the draft is streamed again. With rendered (next_checks), no model call was made: the harness replaced the answer's next-steps section with its rendering of the answer's checked kiwi-next-checks steps, and draft keeps the model's text for review. With rendered (bounded_fallback), a bound ended the request with no diagnosis from the model, and the text that follows is the harness's, written from the request's lookups: returned errors, the cause unknown, no remedy. Its draft is the model's notes streamed before the bound, removed and kept for review: they are not a diagnosis. With rendered (bounded_fallback) and withheld, the model's diagnosis had claim findings and no revision completed: draft is that diagnosis, findings what it was withheld for, and the text that follows is the harness's bounded diagnosis in its place; text a lookup returned that reads as an instruction to the assistant is located there, classed and said not to have been followed, never repeated. With rendered (edit_description), an edit's prose said its proposal kept source comments it removes, or changed only one thing: no model call was made, findings name those sentences, and the text that follows is the answer with them corrected and a harness note naming the removed comment lines; the proposal is unchanged. With rendered (proposal_directive), the accepted proposal carried text written as an instruction to the assistant: no model call was made, findings locate it without repeating it, and the text that follows is the answer with those comments removed from the proposal block and a harness note; the captured proposal is the block without them. Instruction text outside a comment cannot be removed: the block is withheld and the request ends like an edit with no proposal (edit_output_missing). With rendered (claim_settlement), an answer's findings stood after its one revision, or a Kiwi diagnosis written as a bound ended the request had findings and no revision was possible: no model call was made, draft is that answer, findings those that stood, and the text that follows is that answer with each flagged member start line corrected to the returned rows' and each other flagged statement withheld, and a harness note saying what changed. A plain answer is settled only when every finding locates a statement.
oneOf.title: revision

oneOf.description: Protocol 1.5, requests with an editor whose action edits code (diagnose, propose, test_block): how the answer kept contract edit/1. delivered is proposal, no_change or missing; repair is none, repaired, skipped:<bound> or failed:<reason>. Missing ends the request with outcome failed and errorCode edit_output_missing; it is not a refusal. A repaired proposal is made from the accepted block, not from the answer's Markdown, and rendered by the harness after the answer; repairReply keeps the model's raw reply for review. minimalRepair lists how a delivered proposal for one routine or block went past resizing a local variable (deleting it, or rewriting the SELECT ... INTO or RETURN that uses it); the repair then asks once for the smallest change, and only a reply that is one replaces the proposal (otherwise repair is failed:minimal and the first proposal stands). anchorRepair lists %TYPE/%ROWTYPE anchors the supplied schema_metadata shows cannot resolve (an owner and a column without the table); the repair then asks once for corrected anchors, and only a reply whose anchors resolve replaces the proposal (otherwise repair is failed:anchor).
oneOf.title: edit_contract

oneOf.description: Protocol 1.5, Kiwi answers other than the explain actions: the harness's record of the request's lookups, written from the lookups rather than the model's text, sent once before the final budget event. Each entry gives lookup number, callId, operationId, the parameters it ran with, coverage (complete, empty, at_limit, truncated or failed), rows, rowLimit, summary, facts (object status, compiler error locations, waiter and blocker, and source lines read, stated from the rows), subjects (the objects it is about, from its parameters and typed owner/name columns) and sourceRead (per unit, the lines returned and each member shown: declared, or implemented and read whole, in part, or with coverage unknown and why). notRun lists calls the lookup budget stopped. Other row values are not repeated.
oneOf.title: lookup_record

oneOf.description: An answer with code but no proposal (no editor, or no block that could replace it): the fragments a structural check found incomplete, so a pasted repair carries the same warning. Never a compilation.
oneOf.title: code_check

oneOf.description: Provider, model and token usage for the completed request.
oneOf.title: usage

oneOf.description: Terminal event. Always the last event of a successful stream. A Kiwi request that ran out of budget ends with outcome 'partial', partial: true and the stopReason that ended it. An edit request that delivered neither a proposal nor a no-change line ends with outcome 'failed' and errorCode 'edit_output_missing' (1.5); its answer was still streamed.
oneOf.title: done

oneOf.description: Typed failure. The code is stable: disabled, unauthorized, unsupported-version, context-too-large, rate-limit, timeout and provider-failure outcomes all arrive here.
oneOf.title: error

description: The contract between an IDE adapter and the harness copilot API. A major version mismatch is rejected; unknown optional fields are ignored.
guarantees: Applying a proposal updates an editor buffer. It never runs, compiles, commits, or pushes anything.
A proposal is rejected if the document, its revision, the editor, or the target changed since it was generated.
A multi-part proposal applies every part or none: one stale, missing or extra part refuses the whole.
An actor reference asserted by an adapter is namespaced by integration instance and is never treated as a role.
A partially delivered request is never replayed automatically.
Kiwi's lookups are reviewed read-only catalog entries, authorised as the requesting user on every call and recorded as Executions; there is no free-form SQL, write, compile or commit.
Adapters ignore stream events they do not know, so a minor version may add events.
title: OracleDBHarness copilot protocol
